articleTitle: A digital accelerometer for torque-speed studies
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The problem of determining the torque-speed curve of an induction motor is discussed and a digital method is described. Torque-speed curves using three different methods are compared. Improvements to the digital instrument are suggested.

abstract: I would like to thank Prof Hellawell for his remarks. He, however, seems to be pessimistic about the chances of survival of an electrode system in the final application of this method of beach protection. The eddy current electrode would be the obvious choice in this application as it merely consists of a single cable. Experience with communication submarine-cables show that their main source of damage is from trawling activities and dragging anchors. At a sandy beach they become covered by a few metres of sand which protects them against the destructive action of the breakers. The sand very rarely scours out to the ultimate depth of the cable and even then it is exposed for a short period only. Such deep scouring may lake place at roughly 5 year intervals only.

abstract: The calculation of surges on multiconductor lines is complicated by interaction between the surges on the various conductors. Matrix theory for multiconductor lines is summarized and applied to examples on loss-free lines and lines above an imperfect earth. It is shown that wave fronts can be determined in a fairly simple fashion, leading to some insight into the behaviour of a line.

articleTitle: Surge propagation and reflection on a 400kV transmission line
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Two lengths of 400kV three phase transmission line were made available for surge measurements. On a 5 km length low and high voltage measurements were performed. The low voltage oscillograms show various characteristic patterns which can be related to discontinuities on the line. At high voltages the effects of various types of flashover and of corona were evident from comparative oscillograms. Low voltage measurements on a 150 km length of line clearly demonstrate the differing attenuations and propagation velocities of the several modes. A simplified approach to the theory of modes of propagation leads to acceptable explanations for wave front behaviour.

abstract: Advances in component technology, particularly integrated circuits, have now made Pulse Code Modulation economically attractive for use in the junction and trunk areas of telephone and data transmission. This paper reviews the principal parameters of the basic junction system upon which international standardisation is now proceeding. The paper also examines the error noise performance of the system and shows how this differs markedly from Frequency Division Multiplex systems and makes reference to the future developments of the PCM hierarchy.

articleTitle: Logarithmic analogue to digital conversion for processing acoustic signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Two types of logarithmic analogue to digital converters are considered. The operation of the first is based on the discharge of a capacitor through a resistor and the other uses a conventional digital to analogue converter. The former results in a simple low speed converter while the latter is more expensive but is sufficiently fast for sampling audio-frequency signals.

abstract: An electronic system that gives realistic visual demonstration of complexor (phasor) diagrams on the screen of a cathode ray tube is described. One complexor is used as the reference and shown as a horizontal straight line from the centre of the display screen, while the other phasors can be displayed either as a dot on the screen or as a straight line. The dot representation permits the display of complexor loci as test-circuit parameters are altered. The system is designed to work on 50 Hz only.

articleTitle: Maintenance and testing of modern winding plant
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The object of the paper is to assist staff responsible for the maintenance and testing of modern winding plant and to enable them to appreciate the need for a carefully planned maintenance schedule. In general, fundamental principles of winder maintenance are given with certain specific details quoted for the purpose of illustration. Two main classes of the work Involved are dealt with: (1) Dynamic testing and adjusting of equipment, (2) Visual examination and replacement of worn or defective components. Particular attention is given to dynamic testing of mechanical braking systems and safety devices, which are often neglected, and emphasis is placed on maintaining the important aspect of day-to-day output.

articleTitle: The IEC annual general meeting - 1974 - Bucharest - Romania
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The 39th Annual General Meeting of the International Electrotechnical Commission was held from 9-21 September 1974 in Bucharest, Romania. It was attended by some 1 200 delegates and 35 different technical committees were in session. Eight delegates from South Africa attended. At the Council Meeting, Dr V I Popkov was elected President of the IEC. A special meeting was also called to celebrate the 70th Anniversary of the founding of the IEC and it is felt that the speech made by Dr Popkov on this occasion should be of interest to all electrical engineers — particularly since it underlines the disappearance of barriers between the so-called heavy and light current engineering.

abstract: An attempt is made to integrate this subject by bringing together all relevant data from the fields of shark protection, shark biology, neurophysiology, electrical fishing and electrical fish screens. Further tests to determine the conditions for electrotaxis in sharks are described The details of an experiment are given wherein an electrical anti-shark barrier was constructed and tested in the shark infested waters of St Lucia. An account is given of the methods adopted in solving some unusual problems which arose. These include the generation of a uniform electrical field in sea water, corrosion of electrodes, high-efficiency pulse-generation into an inductive load and the low-loss feeding of a low-impedance electrode system at the end of a long transmission line. The entire installation and experiment were carried out with a view to achieving a successful barrier with the minimum wastage of power. A 250 m barrier in 3 m of sea water consumed 35 kW. The experiment showed that electrotaxis is a necessary prerequisite for an electrical field to act as a repellant of harmful sharks.

articleTitle: Communication techniques in deep space tracking
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper discusses in outline the techniques developed over the last decade for the tracking of and acquisition of data from planetary and interplanetary probes launched by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The Deep Space Network of tracking stations including the Hartebeesthoek facility is briefly described. Spacecraft are considered in general terms so that the tracking requirements may be defined. The techniques are then covered in terms of the three basic functions: tracking, telemetry and command. The paper concludes with a short survey of probable developments during the seventies.

articleTitle: Direct digital control of dc machines: The use of z-transform analysis, simulation and compensation techniques for the practical implementation of a DDC system for dc machines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Over the past few years, digital computers have played an ever-increasing role in the field of process control, in a supervising as well as a direct controlling capacity. Direct digital control applications have not been common in electrical engineering applications, owing to the fast sampling rates required. The use of minicomputers specifically for direct digital control purposes may well change this situation, particularly as the cycle time and price of such computers is decreased. This paper describes an actual example of the use of a minicomputer to effect the speed control of a separately excited dc machine. Digital data input and output facilities were used, with a hard-wired interface to effect the phase control of a thyristor bridge, and a digital tachometer. The system was analysed using z-transform methods, and a degree of compensation, based on the sampled-data nature of the system, introduced. The algorithms developed were found to be economical of computer time, because of the use of the hard-wired interface. Two machines were controlled on a time-sharing basis, indicating that this type of application could be considerably extended to use one computer to perform a number of control functions.

articleTitle: Gas insulated energy transmission systems twenty-third bernard price memorial lecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The increasing demand for underground high power electric transmission systems has stimulated the development of new insulating media. Sulphur hexaflouride (SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) has found wide applications for metalclad switchgear up to very high voltages and can also be used to insulate high voltage cables. The SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> molecule tends to form negative ions, which, in turn, leads to high breakdown strength. However, in practical applications considerable reduction of the breakdown voltage may occur due to the movement of free particles and to the shapes and surfaces of the unavoidable insulator spacers. Three-phase gas insulated cables have very favourable electrical parameters and high power transmission capabilities which can exceed 1 000 MVA without artificial cooling. First installations started operating only a few years ago. High voltage testing of gas insulated cables is a special problem because it has to be done on site. The high capacitance of the test object makes it necessary to develop new test techniques to ensure high reliability in service. Finally, attention is given to practical installations of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> insulated transmission systems and expected developments of this very promising new technique as a means to improve the transmission and distribution of electrical energy.

abstract: Mr Hadingham is to be congratulated on his analysis of a device which operates in the saturated region of a magnetic core.
